I’ll read the continuation prompt and the repository’s research workflow, then work through the tasks and save the results in the investigation folder.

The task list includes a strict charge bound that would exclude multiple zeros, so completion will depend on what the analysis actually proves. I’ve split the work into boundary geometry, late-time cap estimates, and a control audit. Each result will be checked before its status is advanced.

A useful result is taking shape: the two simple branches emerging from a hypothetical double admit regular projective tubes over every fixed positive-time interval. Their side flux is exactly zero, and a matching late-cap estimate appears to tend to zero. The key remaining check is the closure: the charge may move to the imaginary-time faces as the caps shrink.

The closure calculation resolves that issue: for this family of windows, the two imaginary-time faces each approach half of the event’s charge while the distant root caps vanish. I’m checking the full error bounds and the higher-multiplicity extension. This gives a precise limit on this approach; it does not exclude a multiple theta zero.

The estimates also extend to fixed imaginary-time width. In that regime, the actual theta root caps approach an explicit nonzero limit, with a controlled error. This supports continuation of the tubes to arbitrarily large finite times. The checks still find no exclusion: the complete boundary retains the charge. I’m saving the derivations and recording the unresolved signed bound in the ledger.

Completed **LHCT-01–03 in their stated scope**, with four [research notes](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/11_late_heat_caps_and_charge_transport/notes/README.md) and an internal review.

The main results are:

- Regular projective tubes continue to arbitrarily large finite times, with every boundary piece accounted for.
- Actual theta caps have explicit error bounds. At fixed imaginary-time width, their limit is nonzero.
- When the late caps shrink to zero, the imaginary-time faces retain the event’s charge—half on each face. This prevents the proposed cap-only argument from excluding a multiple zero.

The geometry and closure results extend to every fixed finite candidate height and multiplicity, with dependent constants.

**The full task list is not complete.** The opposing signed estimate and exclusion tasks, LHCT-05–07, remain unresolved. Their precise missing input and the scoped failure are recorded in the [updated progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/11_late_heat_caps_and_charge_transport/research-progress/01_LATE_HEAT_CAPS_AND_CHARGE_TRANSPORT_PROGRESS_20261022.md). Internal same-model reviews and repository checks passed; no simplicity theorem is claimed.

I was thinking about it, and realized that you could actually use a topology that counts the zeros in addition to the multiple zeros (I think there were such topological invariants studied earlier, the reason we chose one to make zeros give a zero charge is because of the RH -> simple zeros conjecture, see /investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/12_relative_chern_hopf_charges). But since the two caps can cancel each other, it is only the enclosed charge that matters, so only zero creation actually contributes to the loop integral (essentially residues as far as I can tell). This means that if you show that that integral vanishes on the cap and on the sides, then you can show that the integral at t=0 is related directly to the charges created inside. I think this result could be a useful lemma independently of what it proves, and we could use it for future investigations. What do you think?

Regarding how to investigate the large time cap, what I would do is try to quantify how far the zeros are from obeying PCC statistics in some way, perhaps by using the relationship to eigenvalue distribution in a GUE random matrix a la Dyson-Montgomery. Perhaps there is a natural measure of this distribution using some matrix quantity (my guess is a pair distance matrix for pairs of zeros, this actually shows up in the \Delta expression within the Chern-Hopf boundary term we are studying here). If you could quantify this measure precisely, you can try to see how that measure evolves under the heat equation. If it decreased to zero, that would mean that PCC holds asymptotically, so the cap would only have simple zeros, so only the ones created inside would contribute. 

This is a loose argument. Please try to formalize it, create new research-overview and research-progress notes with whatever ideas survive after closer analysis (if any), and then continue with the research.

I’ll check which earlier zero-counting invariants fit your proposed balance law, then test whether a pair-distance statistic can control the late cap. I’ll save the surviving formulation in new overview and progress notes and pursue its first analytical result.
Yes, and also look at investigations-4/09_reciprocal_hodge_energy, that project has been making progress, perhaps it works better in that context too.
I’ll include the reciprocal Hodge energy results, especially any boundary-period or transport identities that could carry the zero count.

The cancellation idea does survive as a useful balance law, and an earlier investigation already proves its real-time version: persistent simple zeros cancel between caps, while real-zero births contribute. The distinction is that a collision does not create complex zeros counted with multiplicity.

The reciprocal Hodge project gives a promising companion: its derivative-weighted energy bounds zero counts when a boundary amplitude is known. I’m working out a regularized counting formula that makes that connection precise and keeps the approximation costs visible.

The pair-distance matrix does yield a concrete result: for any fixed finite block of late theta zeros, its normalized inverse-square matrix converges to an explicit clock matrix. That is a different limit from GUE statistics. Ordinary PCC would also leave sparse exceptional multiple zeros unresolved.

In the Hodge setting, I obtained an exact companion identity: below a certified boundary amplitude, the low-value part of the derivative-weighted energy equals \(4\pi\varepsilon\) times the zero count, including multiplicities. This gives the counting idea a precise analytic form.

The new overview, progress register and four research notes are saved. The Hodge lemma also applies directly to the disk already certified in project 09: its low-value derivative-weighted energy is exactly \(8\pi\varepsilon\), with an explicit positive continuation range in complex heat time.

The reviews caught and corrected a distinction between physical and normalized pair-matrix derivatives. I’m checking links and the final status records now; the complete signed exclusion estimate remains unproved.

The checks passed across 16 updated documents and 465 local links. The new records distinguish the four completed research deliverables from the still-open exclusion estimate, and preserve project 09’s existing results. I’m saving the research history now.

Yes—the cancellation idea yields a useful lemma, and project 09 gives it a concrete analytic form.

- **Real-zero transport:** persistent roots cancel between caps, leaving births and wall crossings:
  \[
  N_{\rm late}-N_{\rm early}+\text{wall flux}
  =2\sum\lfloor m/2\rfloor.
  \]
  Investigation 22 already proves this; I consolidated its precise hypotheses. Complex zeros counted with multiplicity, however, are conserved through collisions.

- **Reciprocal Hodge connection:** I derived
  \[
  2\int_{\Omega\cap\{|H|<\varepsilon\}}
  \frac{|H_z|^2}{|H|}\,dA
  =4\pi\varepsilon N_\Omega,
  \]
  when \(\varepsilon\) is below the boundary amplitude. This counts every multiplicity. Project 09’s certified disk gives an actual theta application, including a positive complex-time continuation range.

- **Pair matrices:** I proved quantitative convergence to a clock matrix for fixed late-time root ranks. A GUE limit would require a different population limit. Weak PCC alone permits sparse exceptional doubles and does not determine cap phase.

Saved the new [research overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/11_late_heat_caps_and_charge_transport/research-overview/02_ZERO_COUNT_TRANSPORT_AND_PAIR_MATRIX_PROGRAM_20261022.md), [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/11_late_heat_caps_and_charge_transport/research-progress/02_ZERO_COUNT_TRANSPORT_AND_PAIR_MATRIX_PROGRESS_20261022.md), four supporting notes and an internal review.

These four scoped deliverables are complete. **The original signed exclusion estimate remains unproved**, so the full original task list is not complete.

Excellent, can you write this up into a detailed manuscript. I think that this result could be interesting in its own right. Please try to write it in a self contained way, focusing on analytic results, checking derivations carefully, and only referencing numerics for backup. You can place this manuscript in the base investigations-4 folder, I think it may be the most interesting result from this series of investigations, and we might want to keep working on it until the result is well characterized, and then move on to a new folder investigations-5. You can put any new research-overview and research-progress files within the base investigations-4 folder as well.

I’ll build a self-contained manuscript around the zero-count transport and Hodge identities, with the pair-matrix results explaining what heat evolution controls. I’ll check the proofs and constants again, keep numerical certificates as supporting examples, and place the manuscript and its overview/progress records in the base investigations-4 folder.

The manuscript’s central result can be stated without RH: localized derivative energy recovers the full zero count below a boundary threshold, even through collisions. I’m also deriving quantitative bounds for its regularization error and extending the identity to finite root covers. Those additions should clarify both its usefulness and its limits.

I’ll use the PDF skill to check the compiled manuscript’s layout as well as its formulas.

The analytic core now includes the original square-root identity and a general formula for \(q\)-fold covers, with explicit error bounds for approximate fields. The theta application also has a self-contained concentration proof from the full source, so its fixed-rank clock limit will not depend on numerical fitting or an imported saddle estimate.

The transport section separately proves the real birth count and the complex discriminant charge, including their different multiplicity weights.

The proof reviews have found no remaining mathematical corrections. I’m now checking the compiled layout and preparing the overview and progress notes, with clear distinctions between established identities, new extensions, and the estimates still needed for the larger program.

The manuscript compiles to 41 pages with no unresolved references or layout warnings. The main proofs stand without numerics; the existing numerical certificate appears only in an appendix. The write-up also makes the key distinction explicit: conserved complex multiplicity, newly appearing real roots, and complex collision residues carry different weights.

The final consistency check passed, including the \(4\pi^2\) normalization and the pair-energy factors. I’m adding the source crosswalk and review record now. The overview also identifies three concrete directions for further work: bounds on the full exterior force, sharper stability of the regularized count, and estimates for the complete physical boundary.

The final PDF has passed compilation and visual inspection. The review records the derivation checks and the corrections made during drafting, including the regularization’s behavior at zero and the boundary orientations. I’m finishing the repository links so the manuscript, progress notes, and source history are easy to follow.

The manuscript and accompanying notes are saved in the base Investigations 4 folder. The final checks found no broken links among the 113 references in the new documents, and the saved PDF matches the checked sources. I’m saving the final research-history record now.
